findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded during web requests, so fallbacks silently fail elsewhere
findings.body: The on-demand locale loader in `I18n.translate` only loads `config.locale` (line 68). The newly added fallback chain is only pre-loaded by `ApplicationController#set_locale` calling `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. Any translation performed outside a controller request — Sidekiq jobs, mailers/user notifications, rake tasks, rails console, middleware that runs before/without the before_filter — will have only the primary locale's YAML loaded, so `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` will look up the fallback locales (site default locale and `:en`) in an empty translation store and still produce a missing translation. The fallback feature therefore works inconsistently depending on the execution context. The loading of the fallback chain should happen inside `load_locale`/`translate` (i.e. whenever a locale is activated) rather than only in the controller filter.

findings.title: Translation LRU cache key does not account for the fallback chain (stale/cross-site translations)
findings.body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With fallbacks enabled, the resolved value for a given (key, locale) pair now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is computed per request in `FallbackLocaleList#[]`. Two consequences: (1) after an admin changes `default_locale`, previously cached fallback results for other locales remain in the process-level LRU cache and keep returning values resolved through the old fallback locale until a reload; (2) in a multisite deployment the LRU cache is shared across all sites in the process while `SiteSetting.default_locale` is per-site, so a string resolved through site A's fallback locale can be served to site B for the same locale/key. The cache key needs to include the fallback chain (or the current site/default locale), or the cache must be invalidated when `default_locale` changes.

findings.title: `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` can raise, and `.uniq.compact` ordering is wrong
findings.body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on `SiteSetting.default_locale` unguarded. If the setting is nil/not yet available (e.g. during asset precompilation, early boot, or before migrations create the site_settings table) this raises `NoMethodError`/DB errors from inside every `I18n.translate` call, since `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` invokes `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on each lookup. Also, `compact` is applied after `uniq`, so a nil `locale` argument is only removed after being compared — the intent (drop nils, then dedupe) would be `.compact.uniq`. Guard the setting lookup (e.g. `SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym`) and reorder.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList#[] recomputes on every lookup, defeating Hash memoization
findings.body: `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` for every translation lookup. Unlike `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`, which memoizes computed chains in the Hash, this override ignores the Hash storage and rebuilds a new array (plus a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read and a `to_sym`) on each call. On a hot path such as rendering a page with many translations this adds an allocation and a site-setting lookup per translation; consider caching per locale (and invalidating when `default_locale` changes).

findings.title: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` assumes a FallbackLocaleList and will 500 if fallbacks are replaced
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` is defined only on the custom `FallbackLocaleList` in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`. If anything else assigns `I18n.fallbacks` (a plugin, or `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` still present in an environment file such as development.rb/test.rb or a deployment's own copy of production.rb, which installs a plain `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks`), this before_filter raises `NoMethodError` on every single request, taking the whole site down. Either define the loading helper in a place that does not depend on the fallbacks object type (e.g. in the translate accelerator, loading `I18n.fallbacks[I18n.locale]`) or guard with `respond_to?`.

findings.title: `@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded! runs outside LOAD_MUTEX
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` lazily initializes and reads `@loaded_locales` without holding `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates the same array under the mutex and `reload!` replaces it. Two threads can both observe nil and each install a fresh array, so a locale recorded as loaded by one thread can be dropped, and `include?` can be executed concurrently with `<<`/reassignment. On non-GVL runtimes this can corrupt the array or cause repeated/missed loads. Initialize `@loaded_locales` eagerly at patch load time or perform the check inside the mutex.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback behaviour
findings.body: This PR introduces a custom fallback chain (user locale → site default locale → :en), moves pluralization setup, and adds `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, yet no specs are added. There is no coverage asserting that a key missing in a user's locale resolves from `SiteSetting.default_locale` and then `:en`, that `FallbackLocaleList#[]` dedupes, or that `ensure_loaded!` actually loads the fallback locale files. Given that fallbacks are now active in all environments (the per-environment `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` lines were removed), regressions here would silently change every missing-translation lookup, including in the test suite where missing translations will now be masked by the :en fallback.
